name: Unpack the packaged game into a private per-user folder
body: A packaged game (D-218) unpacks into `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp/lantern-<fingerprint>`. The name is predictable and `/tmp` is shared, so another user on the same machine can create that folder first (or a symlink to one of theirs) and plant scripts, a shader or a library the next run loads. Unpack into a folder only the running user can write instead: a per-user cache folder (`LANTERN_CACHE_DIRECTORY`, else `LOCALAPPDATA` on Windows, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` on Linux, `~/Library/Caches` on macOS), and only when none of those exists the temp folder under a name with the user in it. Create the `lantern` folder mode 0700 and verify an existing one is not a symlink and is ours before using it. Reuse an unpacked build only when its marker holds the archive's fingerprint, so a start stays fast. Open question: a virtual file system would remove the unpacked copy altogether (D-218's follow-up). Done: see D-224.
acceptance_criteria: The unpack folder is created mode 0700 and is never a symlink
A folder another user created, or a symlink, is refused with a message and the game does not run from it
A second start of the same build reuses the unpacked folder without writing
Windows uses LOCALAPPDATA and skips the POSIX checks
